name: CA-49
label: Safe D

key_factors: Levin holds an overwhelming fundraising edge: $3.2M raised and $1.4M on hand versus under $60K for Kurdian
The district leans Democratic by seven points and Levin is the incumbent
Prediction markets price Levin's win odds at 95-97%
No public polls or expert ratings; outside spending on both sides is negligible
model.rationale: Levin combines a D+7 district, incumbency, and a roughly 50-to-1 fundraising advantage over Kurdian, while markets put his win odds at 95% or higher. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, a comfortable Democratic win is the clear call, shaded slightly below the raw fundamentals because markets are a touch less bullish.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a sharply improved national environment for the GOP could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Levin, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this coastal Southern California district that leans Democratic by seven points. He has raised more than $3.1 million and holds $1.4 million on hand, while Republican Armen Kurdian has raised under $60,000 with almost no outside support. Prediction markets put Levin's win odds between 95% and 97%.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the outlook rests on the district's lean, Levin's incumbency, and his financial dominance in a national environment currently favorable to Democrats. That combination points to a comfortable Levin win, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than who prevails.
